embeds.title: 🔴 New Windows MiniPlasma Zero-Day Exploit Gives System Access, PoC Released
embeds.description:
A researcher known as Chaotic Eclipse released a proof-of-concept exploit for a Windows privilege escalation zero-day called 'MiniPlasma' that claims to give attackers SYSTEM privileges on fully patched Windows systems. The researcher claims the flaw impacts the 'cldflt.sys' Cloud Filter driver and was originally reported to Microsoft by Google Project Zero researcher James Forshaw in September 2020 as CVE-2020-17103, which Microsoft reportedly fixed in December 2020. However, Chaotic Eclipse claims the exact same issue remains unpatched. BleepingComputer tested the exploit on Windows 11 Pro and confirmed it successfully opened a command prompt with SYSTEM privileges. Will Dormann at Tharros also confirmed the exploit works on the latest public version of Windows 11, though it does not work in the Windows 11 Insider Preview Canary build.
**Sources:** BleepingComputer • 🔴 1 corroborating
**CVEs:** CVE-2020-17103, CVE-2026-33825 • **Access:** n/a
**Incident date:** unknown • **Confidence:** claim
[Read source](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/microsoft/new-windows-miniplasma-zero-day-exploit-gives-system-access-poc-released/)
